requirements.evidence: Every contract property and method on Queues is present (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:23-265), and so is accessQueue/accessGrants view data that is null or empty when the queue is foreign (Queues.php:222-237). Rename re-derives the slug: `slug: Str::slug($this->renameName)` (Queues.php:157). The toggle confirmation is an in-page modal (queues.blade.php:95-117). Serve has the scoped findOrFail, the exception-to-notice mapping, an uncaught AuthorizationException, a #[Locked] lastCalledTicketId and a rate limit counting only successful calls (Serve.php:72-111). Members has activeTab/setActiveTab with a whitelist (Members.php:56,265-272) and a role="tablist" tab bar; the invite form appears only on the invites tab (members.blade.php:6-99). Routes and navbar are added (routes/web.php:59-60, default-page.blade.php:44-50). All required lang keys exist in both locales. Gaps: the queue/mode selects use deferred `wire:model` (serve.blade.php:13,23), so the waiting list does not refresh when the selection changes, and the access modal opens on top of the still-active detail modal.

conventions.evidence: Writes go through CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket; #[Validate] + validateOnly is used (Queues.php:29,58,91,152; Serve.php:50,84); authorization uses policies; CHANGELOG and docs/business-rules.md are updated; the markup follows members-page style. Deviations: four modals are written inline instead of as a reusable Blade component; the view uses a fully qualified `\App\Models\UserRole::Owner` (queues.blade.php:134).

security.evidence: Every client id is resolved through `$this->entity->queues()->findOrFail(...)` / `memberships()->findOrFail(...)` before `$this->authorize(...)` (Queues.php:106,128,147,167,183,199,245-248; Serve.php:82-84). Render uses scoped `find` for viewing/access queues (Queues.php:222-228), and Serve only lists tickets for a queue the user may call (Serve.php:143-153). Entity and lastCalledTicketId are #[Locked]; mode is validated with `in:`; the rate limit is per user and entity (Serve.php:87). All output uses {{ }}. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: QueuesTest covers the 403 route for employees, list markup with no per-row actions, create/rename including duplicate-slug and blank errors, the toggle confirmation without wire:confirm, grant/revoke, foreign accessQueueId disclosure, foreign ids raising not-found, and a demoted manager being forbidden on every action (change.diff:1235-1556). ServeTest covers defaults, employee grants, call order/mode/30 limit, the notices, invalid mode, foreign id, unauthorized call, a locked-property tamper and the rate limit (change.diff:1611-1862). Also added: MembersTabsTest, QueueNavigationTest and UiLangKeysTest. Existing tests are adjusted to the tab requirement, not weakened (EntityInviteTest.php:179-185, MembersTest.php:377,397-432).

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean and direct, and setAccess() shares grant/revoke (Queues.php:243-251). Serve::waitingTickets re-implements the ordering and mode filters (`priority > 0` / `priority 0`, Serve.php:160-172) that CallNextTicket presumably already encodes, so the two could drift. The four inline modals repeat the same Bulma modal skeleton.

readability.evidence: Methods are small and well named, with PHPDoc explaining why the untrusted-state properties exist (Queues.php:39-66, Serve.php:43-62). Constants name the rate-limit and list sizes (Serve.php:27-37). There is no dead code or debug output. Minor: the Blade files skip indentation inside the root <div>, and the role check sits inline in the view.

scope.evidence: Every change serves the task: the two components and their views, the Members tabs, routes, navbar, lang keys, docs and changelog, and tests. The only extra key, `serve_rate_limited`, supports the required rate limit. No unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The queue and mode selects use deferred `wire:model`, so changing either one does not re-render the waiting list until another request (such as callNext) is made; `wire:model.live` is needed for the list to follow the selection.
openAccess leaves viewingQueueId set, so the access modal opens stacked on top of the still-active detail modal, and closing it leaves the detail modal open behind it.
The waiting-list query copies the call-order and mode-filter rules instead of reusing the domain definition in CallNextTicket, so the two can drift apart.
Four near-identical Bulma modal blocks are written inline; the conventions prefer extracting repeated markup into an anonymous Blade component.
The role check uses a fully qualified enum class inside the view; an `isManager()`-style helper or a passed variable would be cleaner.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues management page, the Serve panel, the Members tabs, navigation and lang keys. Every action goes through the domain actions, with entity-scoped resolution, policy authorization, locked/validated state and a per-user rate limit. It ships thorough tests, including tamper and unauthorized-call cases. Only minor UX and duplication issues remain (deferred selects not refreshing the waiting list, stacked modals, re-implemented call-order query), so it is approvable with nits.
